info.title: onboard API
info.summary: Config-as-data control plane: client descriptor in, onboarding artifacts out (ADR-0045 P1, ADR-0058).
info.description:
Turns one client descriptor (the CS-Admin source of truth) into the downstream onboarding artifacts, and previews a descriptor's derive/expression rules against sample tags. Generation uses the exact code path of the `onboard-gen` CLI, so both produce byte-identical artifacts.

Served on its own plaintext listener (ONBOARD_API_PORT, default 9105) only when ONBOARD_API_ENABLED=true and ONBOARD_API_KEY is set (the process refuses to start when enabled without a key). Two binaries mount it: the cloud `sparkplug-decoder` container (edge-transformer binary) — the instance edge-api calls via ONBOARD_GENERATE_URL — and, optionally, `sparkplug-agent` on edge boxes (not enabled on the staging agents).

Public exposure: none. No nginx vhost routes to port 9105 on staging or production. In production `sparkplug-decoder` is behind the `client-ingest` compose profile, so it runs only when that profile is enabled.

## How to call this API

- **Auth**: send `Authorization: Bearer <onboard-api-key>` (the shared ONBOARD_API_KEY, not a JWT; the `Bearer` scheme is case-insensitive). A missing or wrong key is 401.
- **Base URLs**: see `servers` — in-network only (`http://sparkplug-decoder:9105`; edge-api reaches it through ONBOARD_GENERATE_URL) and `http://localhost:9105` for local development. Nothing is reachable from the internet.
- **Content types**: `POST /v1/onboard/generate` takes the descriptor as YAML or JSON (the body is parsed as YAML whatever the `Content-Type`); `POST /v1/onboard/simulate` takes JSON. Bodies are capped at ONBOARD_API_MAX_BODY_BYTES (default 4 MiB). Responses are `application/json`.
- **Errors**: handler errors are `application/json` bodies `{"error":"<message>"}` followed by a newline. Descriptor problems are 400 with the parser/validator message (`clientdescriptor: parse: ...` or `clientdescriptor: validate: ...`) so the author can fix them. A wrong HTTP method on a known path is a 405 from Go's router (`text/plain`, `Method Not Allowed`, with an `Allow` header), returned before authentication.
- **Side effects**: none. Both operations are pure functions of the request: they write nothing and publish nothing; the caller stores and applies the returned artifacts. The same request always produces the same response, so retries are safe.
- **Docs**: browse this spec in the API docs portal at https://api.staging.packiot.app/docs/ (behind the cs-admin SSO, read-only Swagger UI). It is also exported to `docs/api/openapi/onboard-api.openapi.json` in packiot-stack-alpha.

servers.description: In-network on packiot-net (alias edge-transformer). Static IP 172.18.0.23:9105 on staging and production.

tags.name: onboard
tags.description: Client-descriptor tooling for onboarding: generate a tenant's configuration artifacts (`generate`) and preview its derived-metric rules against sample readings (`simulate`). Both are stateless.

post.summary: Generate onboarding artifacts from a client descriptor
post.description:
Turns one client descriptor into the tenant's onboarding artifacts: the tenant conversion profile, the topic-registry SQL, the `equipments.position` backfill SQL, the sparkplug-agent config, the Node-RED tee node and, when the descriptor has a `plc` block, the PLC reader `client.yaml` and reader flow (with the descriptor's authored customizations).

**Order of checks**: bearer key (401) → body read under the cap (400 `payload too large` / `cannot read body` / `empty body`) → descriptor parse + validation (400 with the reason) → generation (400 for an authoring error only detectable at render time, e.g. a customization id collision; 500 for any other generator fault) → unmapped-topic check (500 on failure) → 200.

**Mode**: artifacts are always generated in draft/observe mode; cutover readiness is reported in `validation` (`cutover_eligible` is false while any count index is only inferred) instead of blocking generation.

**Side effects**: none — nothing is written to the database or published. The caller (edge-api / CS Admin) stores or applies the artifacts verbatim. Uses the same code path as the `onboard-gen` CLI, so both produce byte-identical artifacts.

**Idempotency**: deterministic; the same descriptor always yields the same response.

**Tenant scoping**: the tenant is whatever the descriptor declares (`tenant`, `enterprise_id`); the shared key authorizes generation for any tenant, so only trusted internal callers hold it.

**Limits**: body ≤ ONBOARD_API_MAX_BODY_BYTES (default 4 MiB). No rate limit.

yamlDescriptor.summary: One machine with a derived scrap count (YAML)
yamlDescriptor.value:
tenant: ACME
enterprise_id: 4200
canonical:
  prefix: ACME/SP
mapping:
  count_index_default_mode: equipment_id
metric_templates:
  member:
    - {leaf: "/Status/MachSpeed", type: double}
agent:
  edge_node_id: acme-edge
  internal_broker: tcp://mosquitto:1883
  raw_topic: acme/raw
  uplink_broker: ssl://ingest.example.invalid:8883
  mtls:
    cert_ref: secret://packiot/staging/acme/uplink-cert
    key_ref: secret://packiot/staging/acme/uplink-key
    ca_ref: secret://packiot/staging/acme/uplink-ca
tee:
  ingest_url: https://localhost:8444/v1/tags
  tls_insecure: true
equipment:
  - topic: ACME/SP/L5/SCRAP
    device_key: dk_047adcb102e15036d985437ae2c0bd12
    id_equipment: 5003
    tp_equipment: 1
    id_unit: 5003
    count_index: {value: 73, confidence: confirmed}
    derived:
      - type: double
        emit:
          - "/Admin/ProdDefectiveCount/{idx}/Unit"
        expr:
          expr: "gross - net"
          vars:
            gross: "/Status/DW0"
            net: "/Status/DW4"

jsonDescriptor.summary: The same descriptor as a JSON object

requestBody.description: The client descriptor itself, as YAML or JSON (JSON is parsed as YAML).

200.description: Artifacts generated (string values; abridged with `…` in this example). `client_yaml` and `reader_flow` appear only for descriptors with a `plc` block.

artifacts.profile_yaml:
tenant: ACME
enterprise_id: 4200
tenant_prefix: ACME/SP
prefix_fixups: []
metric_aliases: []
parameter_aliases: []
parameter_decomposition:
    source_leaf: ""
    params: []
count_index:
    mode: equipment_id
    overrides:
        /L5/SCRAP: 73
metric_templates:
    line: []
    member:
        - leaf: /Status/MachSpeed
          type: double
derived:
    - segment: /L5/SCRAP
      emit:
        - /L5/SCRAP/Admin/ProdDefectiveCount/73/Unit
      type: double
      expr:
        expr: gross - net
        vars:
            gross: /L5/SCRAP/Status/DW0
            net: /L5/SCRAP/Status/DW4
artifacts.register_sql:
-- (abridged) topic-registry rows for tenant ACME (enterprise 4200) — generated from the
-- client descriptor (ADR-0045 P1). DO NOT hand-edit; edit the descriptor + regenerate.
INSERT INTO … (id_enterprise, id_equipment, …, active, id_unit)
VALUES
    (4200, 5003, 'ACME/SP/L5/SCRAP', true, 5003)
ON CONFLICT … WHERE active DO NOTHING;
…
artifacts.position_sql:
-- equipments.position (line flow order) for tenant ACME (enterprise 4200) —
-- generated from the client descriptor (ADR-0045 Bronze). A line's member
-- list order IS the physical infeed→outfeed sequence: first listed = position
-- 1 (infeed), last = outfeed; single-machine cell → position 1. Idempotent.
-- DO NOT hand-edit; edit the descriptor + regenerate.
UPDATE equipments SET position = 1 WHERE id_equipment = 5003 AND tp_equipment = 1;
artifacts.agent_yaml:
sparkplug:
    group_id: ACME
    edge_node_id: acme-edge
    internal_broker: tcp://mosquitto:1883
    raw_topic: acme/raw
    uplink_broker: ssl://ingest.example.invalid:8883
    …
raw_tag_map:
    - metric_suffix: /L5/SCRAP/Status/MachSpeed
      type: double
      device_key: dk_047adcb102e15036d985437ae2c0bd12
      role: speed.nominal
    - metric_suffix: /L5/SCRAP/Admin/ProdDefectiveCount/73/Unit
      type: double
      device_key: dk_047adcb102e15036d985437ae2c0bd12
      role: counter.scrap

400.description: Body problems (`payload too large`, `cannot read body`, `empty body`), a descriptor that does not parse or validate (`clientdescriptor: parse: ...`, `clientdescriptor: validate: ...`), or an authoring error found while rendering (for example a customization id collision). The message is the reason, meant for the descriptor author.

value.error: clientdescriptor: parse: yaml: line 1: did not find expected ',' or ']'

500.description: `generation failed: ...` (a generator fault for a descriptor that passed validation) or `validation failed: ...` (the unmapped-topic check failed). Not the caller's fault; report it.

post.summary: Preview derived-metric rules against sample readings
post.description:
Builds the tenant profile from `descriptor` and feeds `samples`, in order, through the same derive core the `derive-replay` CLI and the edge agent use; each sample is processed as its own one-tag envelope and treated as good quality. Returns the active derived rules (so a preview can show them before any sample) and every tag they synthesized. Used by the CS Admin / customize preview before deploying a descriptor change.

**Order of checks**: bearer key (401) → body read under the cap (400) → JSON decode (400 `invalid JSON body: ...`) → `descriptor` present (400 `missing descriptor`) → descriptor parse + validation (400) → profile build (500 `cannot build profile: ...`) → 200.

**Side effects**: none; nothing is stored or published. Deterministic for the same request.

**Limits**: body ≤ ONBOARD_API_MAX_BODY_BYTES (default 4 MiB). No rate limit; keep `samples` to a preview-sized list.

scrapExpr.summary: Scrap = gross − net over three readings

requestBody.description: A descriptor plus the raw readings to replay through its derived rules.

200.description: Simulation result: the active rules and the tags they produced, in input order. `emitted` is `[]` when nothing fired.

400.description: `payload too large`, `cannot read body`, `empty body`, `invalid JSON body: ...`, `missing descriptor`, or the descriptor's parse/validation message (a descriptor sent as a JSON string instead of an object fails here with a parse error).

value.error: invalid JSON body: unexpected end of JSON input

clientdescriptor: parse: yaml: unmarshal errors:
  line 1: cannot unmarshal !!str `x` into clientdescriptor.Descriptor

500.description: `cannot build profile: ...`: the validated descriptor could not be turned into a tenant profile.

bearerKey.description: `Authorization: Bearer <ONBOARD_API_KEY>` — a shared static key (not a JWT), compared in constant time. Scheme is case-insensitive.

MethodNotAllowed.description: Wrong HTTP method for this path. Produced by Go's router before authentication; carries an `Allow` header.

error.description: Error message; for descriptor problems, the parser/validator reason.

ClientDescriptor.description: Client descriptor (services/sparkplug-decoder/internal/agent/clientdescriptor). Large and evolving, so only the top-level keys are listed; the authoritative shape and validation rules are in clientdescriptor.go.

tenant.description: SparkPlug group_id / enterprise short name, e.g. `ACME`. Required.

mapping.description: Raw -> canonical quirk absorber, copied into the tenant profile.

plc.description: Optional PLC connectivity + tag map; enables `client_yaml` and `reader_flow`. Shape: see clientdescriptor.go.

artifacts.description: Artifacts as strings, to be stored/applied verbatim.

register_sql.description: SQL that registers the generated equipment topics (topic-routing table).

client_yaml.description: PLC reader client.yaml; present only when the descriptor has a `plc` block.

reader_flow.description: Node-RED PLC-reader flow including authored customizations; present only when the descriptor has a `plc` block.

inferred_count_indices.description: Count indices not yet confirmed on a live tee.

items.description: A member whose count index is not yet confirmed on a live tee.

cutover_eligible.description: false when any count index is inferred.

unmapped.description: Descriptor topics that synthesize no canonical metric.

descriptor.description: The client descriptor as a JSON object. (The handler comment mentions a YAML string, but the raw value is parsed as YAML into the descriptor struct, so a JSON string is rejected with 400.)

samples.description: Raw readings replayed in order; each is its own one-tag envelope with good quality.

segment.description: Equipment segment the rule belongs to.

kind.description: Rule shape: `integral` (rate integrated into a counter), `sum` (addends), `expr` (arithmetic expression).

derived_rules.description: Every active derived rule of the profile.

ts_millis.description: Timestamp of the triggering input, unix milliseconds.

after_input.description: Input metric whose arrival produced this tag.

SimulateResponse.description: Rules that ran and the tags they produced.
